title: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan uses AI agents so much, he spends up to $200K a year on tokens
slides: Why does Garry Tan burn $200K on tokens?
The Y Combinator president runs AI agents daily
Most founders still treat tokens as an expense
Your agent budget may soon rival your payroll
Audit one workflow this week: agent or human?
thread_text:
1. $200K on AI tokens?

Garry Tan, president of Y Combinator, burns that much yearly running AI agents daily. Most founders still see tokens as a cost, not a lever.

2. Daily agents, real money

Tan doesn't just experiment—he runs agents every day. That habit turns token spend into a core operating expense, not a side project.

3. Founders stuck on expense

Most still budget tokens like software licenses. But when agents handle real work, the line between expense and investment blurs fast.

4. Payroll's new rival

If agents take over tasks, your token budget could soon match what you pay people. That shift forces a hard look at every workflow.

5. Audit one workflow now

Pick a single task your team does weekly. Ask: could an agent do it? If yes, test it this week. If no, you've learned something.
